second_order: growing and finishing the ace flag
theme_note: These passages mark collective progress along the flag, switch from extending it to maintenance, and ask where effort should go after reaching an edge.

second_order: choosing the flag's lettering, colours, and symbols
theme_note: Participants propose and contest how their own words, gaps, colours, card-suit marks, aro arrow, and freed space should look; what varies is which feature and design they prefer.
regrouped_from: split from an initial crowded-canvas grouping because these passages alter AcePlace's own design, while the neighboring-art theme is held together by dealing with other builders

second_order: negotiating borders, room, and help with neighboring pictures
theme_note: Across distinct exchanges, people ask how works should meet, allow or resist overlap, trade repairs, seek pacts, apologize, concede, and thank one another. The neighboring group and outcome vary; the shared practice is working out coexistence on the crowded canvas.

second_order: calling people to repair and defend shared art
theme_note: These passages recruit a maintenance squad, warn of attacks, identify damage, and call for cleaning or protection. The threatened object and attributed attacker vary, but each mobilizes repairs or defense.

second_order: finding ace community and visibility through making the flag
theme_note: Participants describe flag work as a way to join ace community life, be visibly present, receive outside recognition, and see asexual pride represented. What varies is whether the recognition comes from doing, seeing, praise, or media coverage.

second_order: routing coordination through sidebars, other subs, and Discord
theme_note: People make the location and alliances visible in the sidebar, warn related subreddits, and carry a revised design to another subreddit and its Discord; the venue varies while the practice is moving coordination between named channels.

second_order: placing and repairing pixels with glitches and scripts
theme_note: Participants use a no-cooldown glitch or distribute, explain, and update scripts that check and place pixels. The mechanism varies from an accidental glitch to deliberate automation, but each changes how pixels are placed or repaired.

second_order: correcting old plans and mistaken maintenance
theme_note: These exchanges show defenders undoing a new design, then being told to stop and acknowledging the changed plan. This was separated from attack-defense because the damage is attributed to AcePlace's own outdated or mistaken repair work.
regrouped_from: split from calling people to repair and defend shared art after contrasting claimed attacks with passages that explicitly attribute damage to outdated plans or one's own maintainers

second_order: enlarging the sign to make it visible and defensible
theme_note: Participants propose, coordinate, celebrate, dispute, and defend the enlarged sign. What varies is whether they count success as building bigger, keeping territory, or making the text easier to see and defend.

second_order: thanking, taking stock, and claiming what they made together
theme_note: When the original canvas ends, participants thank placers and lurkers, inspect the surviving sign, recount maintenance, congratulate neighboring heart builders, and name the shared result. The voices vary between AcePlace and Purple Heart participants.

second_order: restarting and maintaining the flag on replacement canvases
theme_note: After r/place ends, people direct others to pxls.space and PlaceTwo, start again, choose between site mechanics, recruit help, report progress, maintain overnight, and fight erasure. The site and technical obstacle vary while the flag-making practice continues.

second_order: debating whether AcePlace still has a point after r/place
theme_note: One late exchange says the room now hosts third-party versions while another says it has no point and doubts open-ended knockoffs will last. This single-exchange theme belongs with no other practice in the record.

second_order: admitting feeling territorial over the flag
theme_note: This single late-found code is the participant's own direct territorial account and belongs with no other practice without turning a feeling into negotiation, defense, or design.
